field_path_semantics.dot_path: Keys such as translations.en.display_name are intended to be merged as nested JSON paths.
field_path_semantics.simple_field: Keys such as display_name_ko are intended to be persisted as direct columns or metadata keys.
field_path_semantics.related_indicators: Array of existing indicator keys intended for calendar-event linkage.

translator_notes: Korean label fields were written for Korean-first UI exposure.
English translation fields were filled only where the request asked for fallback translations.en.* backfill.
User-facing category_label_ko values are semantic labels; they do not require changing the internal category code.
Provider labels are display labels, while provider field values use lowercase/stable provider identifiers.

field_values.translations.en.description: The overnight rate at which U.S. banks lend reserve balances to each other.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It anchors short-term interest rates and reflects the stance of Federal Reserve policy.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher reading usually points to tighter policy and higher funding costs.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower reading usually points to easier policy and lower funding costs.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with 2-year Treasury yields, FedWatch probabilities, inflation data, and FOMC guidance.

field_values.translations.en.description: The market yield on the U.S. Treasury note with a two-year maturity.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It is one of the most policy-sensitive points on the yield curve.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise often signals higher policy-rate expectations or tighter financial conditions.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline often signals lower policy-rate expectations or rising growth concerns.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Watch the spread versus the Fed funds rate, 10-year yield, inflation releases, and FOMC communication.

field_values.translations.en.description: The market yield on the U.S. Treasury note with a ten-year maturity.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It is a benchmark for long-term borrowing costs, valuation discount rates, and global risk pricing.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise can pressure equity valuations and indicate stronger growth, inflation, or term-premium expectations.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline can support duration assets but may also reflect lower growth or risk-off demand.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with inflation expectations, the 2-year yield, the dollar, equities, and credit spreads.

field_values.translations.en.description: The market yield on the U.S. Treasury bond with a thirty-year maturity.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It reflects long-horizon growth, inflation, fiscal, and term-premium expectations.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise can tighten financial conditions and weigh on long-duration assets.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline can ease long-term discount rates but may also indicate defensive demand.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Check the 10-year yield, inflation trends, Treasury supply, and curve steepening or flattening.

field_values.translations.en.description: The difference between the U.S. 10-year and 2-year Treasury yields.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It helps summarize the slope of the yield curve and the market's growth-policy mix.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher spread usually means curve steepening, often linked to better growth expectations or higher term premium.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower or negative spread signals flattening or inversion, often linked to tight policy or recession concern.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Interpret alongside the level of yields, Fed policy expectations, inflation data, and credit spreads.

field_values.translations.en.description: A broad measure of the cost of overnight borrowing collateralized by U.S. Treasury securities.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It is a key reference rate for dollar funding and many floating-rate instruments.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher rate points to tighter short-term funding conditions.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower rate points to easier short-term funding conditions.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Watch quarter-end effects, repo-market stress, Fed policy, and the spread against policy rates.

field_values.translations.en.description: A broad measure of prices paid by U.S. consumers for goods and services.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It is a major input for inflation expectations and Federal Reserve policy pricing.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher reading suggests stronger inflation pressure and can weaken rate-cut expectations.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower reading suggests easing inflation pressure and can support easier-policy expectations.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Focus on core components, shelter, energy, month-over-month momentum, and market reaction in yields and the dollar.

field_values.translations.en.description: The personal consumption expenditures price index excluding food and energy.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It is the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher reading can signal persistent inflation and a more restrictive policy path.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower reading can support confidence that inflation is cooling.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with CPI, wage growth, personal income, spending data, and Fed guidance.

field_values.translations.en.description: The share of the U.S. labor force that is unemployed and actively seeking work.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It is a key measure of labor-market slack and recession risk.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher rate can indicate labor-market weakening and slower growth.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower rate can indicate a tight labor market and potential wage pressure.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Interpret with payroll growth, participation, jobless claims, wage growth, and revisions.

field_values.translations.en.description: The weekly number of people filing first-time claims for unemployment insurance.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It provides a timely read on labor-market deterioration or resilience.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher reading can signal rising layoffs and weaker labor demand.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower reading can signal resilient employment conditions.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Use the four-week average and compare with unemployment, payrolls, and recession-sensitive assets.

field_values.translations.en.description: A composite indicator designed to signal future turns in the U.S. business cycle.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It helps investors assess whether growth momentum is improving or weakening.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher reading suggests improving forward economic momentum.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower reading suggests weakening forward economic momentum.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Watch the trend over several months and compare with credit spreads, yields, and equity breadth.

field_values.translations.en.description: A broad measure of U.S. money supply including cash, checking deposits, savings deposits, and similar liquid money.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It provides context on liquidity conditions and monetary transmission.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: Faster growth may indicate improving liquidity, though the market impact depends on inflation and credit conditions.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: Contraction or slower growth may indicate tighter liquidity and weaker credit creation.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with bank lending, inflation, policy rates, and risk-asset performance.

field_values.translations.en.description: The option-adjusted spread of U.S. high-yield corporate bonds over comparable Treasuries.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It is a key gauge of credit stress and risk appetite.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher spread indicates rising default concern and weaker risk sentiment.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower spread indicates stronger credit appetite and easier financing conditions.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with equity volatility, investment-grade spreads, Treasury yields, and recession indicators.

field_values.translations.en.description: The option-adjusted spread of U.S. investment-grade corporate bonds over comparable Treasuries.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It tracks credit conditions for higher-quality corporate borrowers.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher spread signals tighter credit conditions and rising risk premia.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower spread signals easier credit conditions and stronger investor demand.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Watch alongside high-yield spreads, Treasury yields, equity volatility, and liquidity conditions.

field_values.translations.en.description: A broad U.S. large-cap equity index.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It is the primary benchmark for U.S. equity risk appetite.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher index level generally reflects stronger equity demand and risk appetite.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower index level generally reflects weaker risk appetite or earnings/valuation pressure.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with sector leadership, Treasury yields, VIX, credit spreads, and earnings expectations.

field_values.translations.en.description: A U.S. equity index with heavy exposure to technology and growth companies.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It is sensitive to growth expectations, discount rates, and technology-sector sentiment.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise can indicate strong demand for growth and technology shares.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline can indicate pressure from higher rates, weaker risk appetite, or tech-specific concerns.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with 10-year yields, XLK, S&P 500, and earnings news.

field_values.translations.en.description: South Korea's main equity-market index.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It reflects Korean equity-market sentiment and global trade-cycle exposure.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise suggests stronger demand for Korean equities and cyclical exposure.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline suggests weaker risk appetite or pressure from global growth, FX, or semiconductor cycles.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Watch USD/KRW, global technology shares, China data, and foreign investor flows.

field_values.translations.en.description: A leading Japanese equity index composed of major listed companies.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It reflects Japanese equity sentiment and global cyclical risk appetite.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise suggests stronger investor demand for Japanese equities.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline suggests weaker equity sentiment or pressure from currency and rate moves.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with USD/JPY, global equities, Bank of Japan expectations, and export-sector trends.

field_values.translations.en.description: Germany's major blue-chip equity index.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It reflects European cyclical, export, and industrial-market sentiment.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise suggests stronger European risk appetite and cyclical expectations.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline suggests weaker growth sentiment or pressure from rates, energy, or currency moves.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Watch EUR/USD, European yields, energy prices, and global manufacturing data.

field_values.translations.en.description: A broad index of stocks listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It provides a read on mainland China equity sentiment.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise can indicate stronger domestic risk appetite or policy-support expectations.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline can indicate weaker growth confidence or policy disappointment.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with China credit data, commodities, USD/CNY, and Asian equity markets.

field_values.translations.en.description: A market-implied measure of expected S&P 500 volatility.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It is widely used as a gauge of equity-market fear and hedging demand.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher VIX usually signals rising uncertainty or risk-off conditions.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower VIX usually signals calmer markets and lower demand for downside protection.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with S&P 500 moves, credit spreads, event risk, and options-expiration effects.

field_values.translations.en.description: An index measuring the U.S. dollar against a basket of major currencies.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It summarizes broad dollar strength and global liquidity pressure.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher index indicates a stronger dollar, often tightening conditions for global risk assets.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower index indicates a weaker dollar, often easing pressure on non-U.S. assets.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with U.S. yields, EUR/USD, USD/JPY, commodities, and risk sentiment.

field_values.translations.en.description: The front-month futures price for West Texas Intermediate crude oil.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It is a key signal for energy prices, inflation pressure, and global demand expectations.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher price can reflect stronger demand, supply disruption, or inflation pressure.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower price can reflect weaker demand, higher supply, or easing inflation pressure.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with Brent, the dollar, inventory data, geopolitical risk, and energy-sector performance.

field_values.translations.en.description: The front-month futures price for gold.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: Gold is watched as a real-rate, dollar, and safe-haven sensitive asset.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher price can signal stronger safe-haven demand, lower real yields, or a weaker dollar.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower price can signal higher real yields, a stronger dollar, or reduced defensive demand.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with real yields, DXY, inflation expectations, and risk sentiment.

field_values.translations.en.description: The front-month futures price for copper.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: Copper is a cyclical commodity often used as a gauge of industrial demand.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher price can signal stronger manufacturing or infrastructure demand.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower price can signal weaker industrial demand or stronger supply pressure.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with China data, manufacturing PMIs, the dollar, and the copper/gold ratio.

field_values.translations.en.description: The exchange rate between the U.S. dollar and the Korean won.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It is important for Korean investors because it affects imported inflation, foreign flows, and global risk sensitivity.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher rate means a stronger dollar or weaker won, often linked to risk-off pressure.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower rate means a stronger won or weaker dollar, often linked to improved risk appetite.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with DXY, U.S. yields, KOSPI, China data, and foreign investor flows.

field_values.translations.en.description: The exchange rate between the euro and the U.S. dollar.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It is the main currency pair for comparing euro-area and U.S. macro expectations.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher rate means a stronger euro or weaker dollar.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower rate means a weaker euro or stronger dollar.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Watch U.S.-Europe rate differentials, ECB and Fed guidance, DXY, and energy-market pressures.

field_values.translations.en.description: The exchange rate between the U.S. dollar and the Japanese yen.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It reflects rate differentials, dollar strength, and yen funding conditions.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher rate means a stronger dollar or weaker yen.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower rate means a weaker dollar or stronger yen.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with U.S. yields, Bank of Japan expectations, Nikkei performance, and risk sentiment.

field_values.translations.en.description: A ratio comparing copper prices with gold prices.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It is used as a rough gauge of cyclical growth appetite versus defensive demand.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher ratio suggests stronger cyclical or industrial-demand sentiment.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower ratio suggests more defensive demand or weaker growth expectations.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with Treasury yields, China data, manufacturing indicators, and equity cyclicals.

field_values.translations.en.description: The price difference between WTI crude and Brent crude.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It helps identify relative U.S. versus global crude-market tightness.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher spread can mean WTI is strengthening versus Brent or the discount is narrowing.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower spread can mean WTI is weakening versus Brent or the discount is widening.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Check inventory data, export constraints, geopolitics, refinery demand, and the overall oil-price trend.

field_values.translations.en.description: A U.S. equity sector ETF proxy for technology companies.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It shows leadership or weakness in technology shares within the broader market.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise suggests stronger demand for technology and growth exposure.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline suggests weaker technology sentiment or pressure from rates and earnings.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with NASDAQ, 10-year yields, semiconductors, and earnings revisions.

field_values.translations.en.description: A U.S. equity sector ETF proxy for banks, insurers, and financial companies.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It reflects credit conditions, yield-curve expectations, and financial-sector sentiment.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise can signal stronger confidence in banks, credit, or net-interest-margin expectations.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline can signal concern about credit quality, curve pressure, or financial stress.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with yield-curve slope, credit spreads, bank earnings, and regulatory news.

field_values.translations.en.description: A U.S. equity sector ETF proxy for energy companies.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It tracks equity-market exposure to oil, gas, and energy-cycle expectations.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise often reflects stronger energy prices or improved energy-sector sentiment.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline often reflects weaker commodity prices or demand concerns.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with WTI, Brent, the dollar, inventories, and geopolitical risk.

field_values.translations.en.description: A U.S. equity sector ETF proxy for health care companies.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It is often viewed as a defensive sector with policy and earnings-specific drivers.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise can indicate defensive demand or stronger sector fundamentals.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline can indicate rotation away from defensives or sector-specific pressure.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with broad equity sentiment, policy risk, earnings, and factor rotation.

field_values.translations.en.description: A U.S. equity sector ETF proxy for industrial companies.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It reflects cyclical growth, capital spending, and manufacturing expectations.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise suggests stronger cyclical and industrial demand expectations.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline suggests weaker manufacturing or capital-spending sentiment.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with ISM data, durable goods, copper, yields, and global trade indicators.

field_values.translations.en.description: A U.S. equity sector ETF proxy for consumer discretionary companies.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It reflects consumer confidence, spending appetite, and growth-stock exposure.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise suggests stronger discretionary spending expectations or risk appetite.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline suggests consumer caution, rate pressure, or weaker growth expectations.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with retail sales, labor data, consumer sentiment, rates, and earnings.

field_values.translations.en.description: A U.S. equity sector ETF proxy for consumer staples companies.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It is often used as a defensive equity-sector benchmark.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise can reflect defensive demand or stable earnings preference.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline can reflect rotation toward cyclicals or sector-specific weakness.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with XLY, inflation data, margins, and broad risk appetite.

field_values.translations.en.description: A U.S. equity sector ETF proxy for utility companies.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It is rate-sensitive and often treated as a defensive, dividend-oriented sector.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise can indicate defensive demand or lower-yield support.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline can indicate higher-rate pressure or rotation into cyclicals.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with Treasury yields, dividend factors, risk sentiment, and power-demand trends.

field_values.translations.en.description: A U.S. equity sector ETF proxy for materials companies.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It reflects demand for chemicals, metals, construction inputs, and global cyclical activity.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise suggests stronger cyclical or commodity-linked demand expectations.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline suggests weaker global growth or commodity demand expectations.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with copper, China data, manufacturing indicators, and the dollar.

field_values.translations.en.description: A U.S. equity sector ETF proxy for real estate companies and REITs.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It is sensitive to interest rates, financing costs, and property-market expectations.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise can indicate lower-rate support or stronger property-sector sentiment.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline can indicate higher-rate pressure or concern about real-estate fundamentals.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with 10-year yields, credit conditions, housing data, and dividend factors.

field_values.translations.en.description: A U.S. equity sector ETF proxy for communication services companies.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It includes media, telecom, and large platform businesses with growth and advertising exposure.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise suggests stronger demand for communication-platform and media exposure.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline suggests weaker growth, advertising, or platform-sector sentiment.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with NASDAQ, technology shares, advertising trends, yields, and earnings.

field_values.translations.en.description: The date of the next Federal Open Market Committee meeting that will set the policy-rate decision and guidance.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It anchors the timing of policy expectations across rates, FX, equities, and bonds.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: For a date field, the key signal is not high or low but how close the meeting is and how expectations change before it.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: For a date field, the key signal is not high or low but how close the meeting is and how expectations change before it.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Around the meeting, track FedWatch probabilities, 2-year yields, statement wording, and press-conference guidance.

field_values.translations.en.description: The policy-rate level decided at an FOMC meeting.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It allows markets to compare the actual policy decision with expectations priced before the meeting.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher-than-expected decision is generally a hawkish surprise and can tighten financial conditions.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower-than-expected decision is generally a dovish surprise and can support liquidity expectations.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: The rate level should be read together with the statement, dot plot, press conference, and forward guidance.

field_values.translations.en.description: The size of the policy-rate change at the meeting, measured in basis points.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It captures the intensity of the policy move and the surprise versus market expectations.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A larger hike or smaller cut than expected can be interpreted as a hawkish surprise.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A larger cut or smaller hike than expected can be interpreted as a dovish surprise.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Clearly define the sign convention in the UI and compare with pre-meeting FedWatch pricing.

field_values.translations.en.description: The market-implied probability that the Fed keeps the policy rate unchanged at a target meeting.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It summarizes rate-market expectations before FOMC decisions.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher probability indicates stronger expectations for no policy-rate change.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower probability indicates rising expectations for a cut or hike instead of a hold.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with 2-year yields, inflation data, labor data, and Fed communication.

field_values.translations.en.description: The market-implied probability that the Fed cuts the policy rate at a target meeting.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It tracks how strongly markets expect policy easing.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher probability signals stronger expectations for easier policy.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower probability signals reduced expectations for easing.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with inflation surprises, labor-market weakness, recession risk, and FOMC communication.

field_values.translations.en.description: The market-implied probability that the Fed raises the policy rate at a target meeting.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It tracks how strongly markets expect policy tightening.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher probability signals stronger expectations for tighter policy.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower probability signals reduced expectations for additional tightening.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with inflation pressure, wage data, 2-year yields, and FOMC communication.

field_values.translations.en.description: A major inflation release that measures changes in prices paid by consumers for goods and services.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: Markets watch CPI because high inflation can reduce rate-cut expectations and pressure risk assets.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A stronger-than-expected release can be read as persistent inflation pressure and may push yields higher.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A weaker-than-expected release can be read as easing inflation pressure and may support easier-policy expectations.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Focus on core CPI, shelter, services inflation, and the immediate reaction in 2-year yields, the dollar, and equity futures.

field_values.translations.en.description: A producer-price release that measures price changes faced by businesses at the production stage.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It helps markets assess whether upstream cost pressure may pass through to consumer inflation.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A stronger-than-expected release can raise concern about future inflation pressure.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A weaker-than-expected release can suggest easing cost pressure for businesses.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with CPI, commodity prices, Treasury yields, and dollar moves.

field_values.translations.en.display_name: U.S. PCE Inflation / Personal Income and Outlays
field_values.translations.en.description: A release covering the Fed-preferred PCE inflation measures together with personal income and spending.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: Core PCE is closely tied to Fed policy assessment, so markets react strongly to surprises.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A stronger-than-expected release can make the Fed less confident that inflation is cooling.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A weaker-than-expected release can improve confidence that inflation is moving toward target.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Focus on core PCE, income, spending momentum, revisions, FedWatch pricing, and the yield-curve reaction.

field_values.translations.en.description: The main U.S. labor-market release covering nonfarm payrolls, unemployment, and wage growth.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It can change expectations for growth, inflation, and the Fed policy path.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: Stronger job or wage data can signal resilient demand and potential inflation pressure.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: Weaker job or wage data can signal labor-market cooling and slower growth.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Read payrolls, unemployment, participation, average hourly earnings, revisions, and the reaction in yields and equities together.

field_values.translations.en.description: A weekly release showing first-time filings for unemployment insurance.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It is one of the timeliest indicators of labor-market stress.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher-than-expected reading can point to rising layoffs and weaker labor demand.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower-than-expected reading can point to resilient labor demand.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Use the four-week average and compare with the unemployment rate, payroll trend, yields, and equity reaction.

field_values.translations.en.description: A labor-market release covering job openings, quits, hires, and separations.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It helps markets assess labor demand and wage-pressure risks beyond payrolls.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A stronger-than-expected reading can indicate tight labor conditions.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A weaker-than-expected reading can indicate cooling labor demand.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Focus on job openings, quits, revisions, and consistency with claims, unemployment, and wage data.

field_values.translations.en.description: A broad release measuring the inflation-adjusted value of goods and services produced in the U.S. economy.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It is the main benchmark for overall growth momentum.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A stronger-than-expected release can signal resilient growth and support cyclical assets, but may also affect rate expectations.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A weaker-than-expected release can signal growth slowdown and increase defensive demand.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Look at real final sales, consumption, inventories, inflation components, revisions, yields, and equity leadership.

field_values.translations.en.description: A monthly release tracking sales by retailers and providing a timely view of consumer spending.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It is important because consumption is a large part of U.S. economic activity.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A stronger-than-expected release can signal resilient consumer demand.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A weaker-than-expected release can signal consumer caution or slowing demand.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Focus on the control group, revisions, inflation effects, consumer discretionary shares, and rates.

field_values.translations.en.description: A release measuring new orders for long-lasting manufactured goods.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It helps assess business investment, manufacturing demand, and cyclical momentum.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A stronger-than-expected release can indicate improving capital-spending and manufacturing demand.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A weaker-than-expected release can indicate softer business investment or manufacturing momentum.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Watch core capital-goods orders, aircraft volatility, revisions, industrials, copper, and yields.

field_values.translations.en.description: A monthly release showing the number of new residential construction projects started.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It is a rate-sensitive indicator of housing activity and construction momentum.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A stronger-than-expected release can suggest resilient housing demand or construction activity.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A weaker-than-expected release can suggest pressure from mortgage rates or slower housing demand.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with permits, mortgage-rate proxies, 10-year yields, homebuilder sentiment, and real-estate equities.

field_values.translations.en.description: A monthly release showing sales of newly built single-family homes.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It provides a read on housing demand and household confidence in a rate-sensitive sector.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A stronger-than-expected release can signal resilient housing demand.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A weaker-than-expected release can signal affordability pressure or weaker housing activity.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with mortgage-rate proxies, housing starts, homebuilder sentiment, 10-year yields, and real-estate equities.

field_values.translations.en.description: A survey-based indicator of U.S. manufacturing activity.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It is watched for early signals on cyclical growth, orders, prices, and employment.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A stronger-than-expected release can indicate improving manufacturing momentum.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A weaker-than-expected release can indicate contracting or slowing manufacturing conditions.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Focus on new orders, prices paid, employment, inventories, industrials, copper, and yields.

field_values.translations.en.description: A survey-based indicator of U.S. services-sector activity.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: Services drive a large share of the U.S. economy and inflation pressure.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A stronger-than-expected release can signal resilient demand and possible services inflation pressure.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A weaker-than-expected release can signal cooling demand in the services sector.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Focus on business activity, new orders, employment, prices paid, yields, and equity-sector reaction.

field_values.translations.en.description: A Federal Reserve policy meeting where the committee sets the policy-rate decision and communicates its outlook.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It is one of the most important events for rates, FX, equities, and credit markets.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A more hawkish decision or message can tighten financial conditions.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A more dovish decision or message can ease financial conditions.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Compare the decision with FedWatch pricing, statement wording, dot plot, press conference, and moves in 2-year yields.

field_values.translations.en.description: The detailed record of a previous FOMC meeting's discussion.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It helps markets interpret the committee's reaction function and balance of risks.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: More hawkish minutes can raise expected policy restrictiveness.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: More dovish minutes can lower expected policy restrictiveness.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Watch language on inflation, labor markets, financial conditions, balance sheet policy, and the reaction in yields and the dollar.

field_values.translations.en.description: The monthly expiration of listed options contracts, often concentrated on the third Friday of the month.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It can affect short-term equity index flows, hedging demand, and volatility around expiration.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A larger expiration with strong dealer-positioning effects can amplify short-term moves.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A smaller or less concentrated expiration may have a more limited market impact.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Track S&P 500, NASDAQ, VIX, index levels versus large option strikes, and post-expiration liquidity.

field_values.translations.en.description: A quarterly expiration date when stock options, stock-index futures, and stock-index options expire together.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It can increase volume, rebalance flows, and short-term volatility in equity markets.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: Large positioning into expiration can amplify index or sector moves.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: Light positioning or offsetting flows can reduce the visible market impact.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Watch S&P 500, NASDAQ, VIX, sector ETFs, futures rolls, and closing-auction volume.

field_values.translations.en.description: A survey release measuring households' views on current conditions, expectations, and inflation.
field_values.translations.en.market_role: It helps markets assess consumer confidence and inflation expectations.
field_values.translations.en.higher_meaning: A stronger-than-expected release can signal resilient consumer confidence.
field_values.translations.en.lower_meaning: A weaker-than-expected release can signal consumer caution or weaker spending intentions.
field_values.translations.en.watch_points: Focus on inflation-expectations components, current conditions, expectations, retail sales, and consumer-discretionary stocks.

DFF.translations.en.description: The overnight rate at which U.S. banks lend reserve balances to each other.
DFF.translations.en.market_role: It anchors short-term interest rates and reflects the stance of Federal Reserve policy.
DFF.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher reading usually points to tighter policy and higher funding costs.
DFF.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower reading usually points to easier policy and lower funding costs.
DFF.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with 2-year Treasury yields, FedWatch probabilities, inflation data, and FOMC guidance.

DGS2.translations.en.description: The market yield on the U.S. Treasury note with a two-year maturity.
DGS2.translations.en.market_role: It is one of the most policy-sensitive points on the yield curve.
DGS2.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise often signals higher policy-rate expectations or tighter financial conditions.
DGS2.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline often signals lower policy-rate expectations or rising growth concerns.
DGS2.translations.en.watch_points: Watch the spread versus the Fed funds rate, 10-year yield, inflation releases, and FOMC communication.

DGS10.translations.en.description: The market yield on the U.S. Treasury note with a ten-year maturity.
DGS10.translations.en.market_role: It is a benchmark for long-term borrowing costs, valuation discount rates, and global risk pricing.
DGS10.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise can pressure equity valuations and indicate stronger growth, inflation, or term-premium expectations.
DGS10.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline can support duration assets but may also reflect lower growth or risk-off demand.
DGS10.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with inflation expectations, the 2-year yield, the dollar, equities, and credit spreads.

DGS30.translations.en.description: The market yield on the U.S. Treasury bond with a thirty-year maturity.
DGS30.translations.en.market_role: It reflects long-horizon growth, inflation, fiscal, and term-premium expectations.
DGS30.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise can tighten financial conditions and weigh on long-duration assets.
DGS30.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline can ease long-term discount rates but may also indicate defensive demand.
DGS30.translations.en.watch_points: Check the 10-year yield, inflation trends, Treasury supply, and curve steepening or flattening.

T10Y2Y.translations.en.description: The difference between the U.S. 10-year and 2-year Treasury yields.
T10Y2Y.translations.en.market_role: It helps summarize the slope of the yield curve and the market's growth-policy mix.
T10Y2Y.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher spread usually means curve steepening, often linked to better growth expectations or higher term premium.
T10Y2Y.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower or negative spread signals flattening or inversion, often linked to tight policy or recession concern.
T10Y2Y.translations.en.watch_points: Interpret alongside the level of yields, Fed policy expectations, inflation data, and credit spreads.

SOFR.translations.en.description: A broad measure of the cost of overnight borrowing collateralized by U.S. Treasury securities.
SOFR.translations.en.market_role: It is a key reference rate for dollar funding and many floating-rate instruments.
SOFR.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher rate points to tighter short-term funding conditions.
SOFR.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower rate points to easier short-term funding conditions.
SOFR.translations.en.watch_points: Watch quarter-end effects, repo-market stress, Fed policy, and the spread against policy rates.

CPIAUCSL.translations.en.description: A broad measure of prices paid by U.S. consumers for goods and services.
CPIAUCSL.translations.en.market_role: It is a major input for inflation expectations and Federal Reserve policy pricing.
CPIAUCSL.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher reading suggests stronger inflation pressure and can weaken rate-cut expectations.
CPIAUCSL.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower reading suggests easing inflation pressure and can support easier-policy expectations.
CPIAUCSL.translations.en.watch_points: Focus on core components, shelter, energy, month-over-month momentum, and market reaction in yields and the dollar.

PCEPILFE.translations.en.description: The personal consumption expenditures price index excluding food and energy.
PCEPILFE.translations.en.market_role: It is the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge.
PCEPILFE.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher reading can signal persistent inflation and a more restrictive policy path.
PCEPILFE.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower reading can support confidence that inflation is cooling.
PCEPILFE.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with CPI, wage growth, personal income, spending data, and Fed guidance.

UNRATE.translations.en.description: The share of the U.S. labor force that is unemployed and actively seeking work.
UNRATE.translations.en.market_role: It is a key measure of labor-market slack and recession risk.
UNRATE.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher rate can indicate labor-market weakening and slower growth.
UNRATE.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower rate can indicate a tight labor market and potential wage pressure.
UNRATE.translations.en.watch_points: Interpret with payroll growth, participation, jobless claims, wage growth, and revisions.

ICSA.translations.en.description: The weekly number of people filing first-time claims for unemployment insurance.
ICSA.translations.en.market_role: It provides a timely read on labor-market deterioration or resilience.
ICSA.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher reading can signal rising layoffs and weaker labor demand.
ICSA.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower reading can signal resilient employment conditions.
ICSA.translations.en.watch_points: Use the four-week average and compare with unemployment, payrolls, and recession-sensitive assets.

USSLIND.translations.en.description: A composite indicator designed to signal future turns in the U.S. business cycle.
USSLIND.translations.en.market_role: It helps investors assess whether growth momentum is improving or weakening.
USSLIND.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher reading suggests improving forward economic momentum.
USSLIND.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower reading suggests weakening forward economic momentum.
USSLIND.translations.en.watch_points: Watch the trend over several months and compare with credit spreads, yields, and equity breadth.

M2SL.translations.en.description: A broad measure of U.S. money supply including cash, checking deposits, savings deposits, and similar liquid money.
M2SL.translations.en.market_role: It provides context on liquidity conditions and monetary transmission.
M2SL.translations.en.higher_meaning: Faster growth may indicate improving liquidity, though the market impact depends on inflation and credit conditions.
M2SL.translations.en.lower_meaning: Contraction or slower growth may indicate tighter liquidity and weaker credit creation.
M2SL.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with bank lending, inflation, policy rates, and risk-asset performance.

HY_OAS.translations.en.description: The option-adjusted spread of U.S. high-yield corporate bonds over comparable Treasuries.
HY_OAS.translations.en.market_role: It is a key gauge of credit stress and risk appetite.
HY_OAS.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher spread indicates rising default concern and weaker risk sentiment.
HY_OAS.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower spread indicates stronger credit appetite and easier financing conditions.
HY_OAS.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with equity volatility, investment-grade spreads, Treasury yields, and recession indicators.

IG_OAS.translations.en.description: The option-adjusted spread of U.S. investment-grade corporate bonds over comparable Treasuries.
IG_OAS.translations.en.market_role: It tracks credit conditions for higher-quality corporate borrowers.
IG_OAS.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher spread signals tighter credit conditions and rising risk premia.
IG_OAS.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower spread signals easier credit conditions and stronger investor demand.
IG_OAS.translations.en.watch_points: Watch alongside high-yield spreads, Treasury yields, equity volatility, and liquidity conditions.

^GSPC.translations.en.description: A broad U.S. large-cap equity index.
^GSPC.translations.en.market_role: It is the primary benchmark for U.S. equity risk appetite.
^GSPC.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher index level generally reflects stronger equity demand and risk appetite.
^GSPC.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower index level generally reflects weaker risk appetite or earnings/valuation pressure.
^GSPC.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with sector leadership, Treasury yields, VIX, credit spreads, and earnings expectations.

^IXIC.translations.en.description: A U.S. equity index with heavy exposure to technology and growth companies.
^IXIC.translations.en.market_role: It is sensitive to growth expectations, discount rates, and technology-sector sentiment.
^IXIC.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise can indicate strong demand for growth and technology shares.
^IXIC.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline can indicate pressure from higher rates, weaker risk appetite, or tech-specific concerns.
^IXIC.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with 10-year yields, XLK, S&P 500, and earnings news.

^KS11.translations.en.market_role: It reflects Korean equity-market sentiment and global trade-cycle exposure.
^KS11.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise suggests stronger demand for Korean equities and cyclical exposure.
^KS11.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline suggests weaker risk appetite or pressure from global growth, FX, or semiconductor cycles.
^KS11.translations.en.watch_points: Watch USD/KRW, global technology shares, China data, and foreign investor flows.

^N225.translations.en.description: A leading Japanese equity index composed of major listed companies.
^N225.translations.en.market_role: It reflects Japanese equity sentiment and global cyclical risk appetite.
^N225.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise suggests stronger investor demand for Japanese equities.
^N225.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline suggests weaker equity sentiment or pressure from currency and rate moves.
^N225.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with USD/JPY, global equities, Bank of Japan expectations, and export-sector trends.

^GDAXI.translations.en.market_role: It reflects European cyclical, export, and industrial-market sentiment.
^GDAXI.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise suggests stronger European risk appetite and cyclical expectations.
^GDAXI.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline suggests weaker growth sentiment or pressure from rates, energy, or currency moves.
^GDAXI.translations.en.watch_points: Watch EUR/USD, European yields, energy prices, and global manufacturing data.

^SSEC.translations.en.description: A broad index of stocks listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange.
^SSEC.translations.en.market_role: It provides a read on mainland China equity sentiment.
^SSEC.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise can indicate stronger domestic risk appetite or policy-support expectations.
^SSEC.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline can indicate weaker growth confidence or policy disappointment.
^SSEC.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with China credit data, commodities, USD/CNY, and Asian equity markets.

^VIX.translations.en.description: A market-implied measure of expected S&P 500 volatility.
^VIX.translations.en.market_role: It is widely used as a gauge of equity-market fear and hedging demand.
^VIX.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher VIX usually signals rising uncertainty or risk-off conditions.
^VIX.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower VIX usually signals calmer markets and lower demand for downside protection.
^VIX.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with S&P 500 moves, credit spreads, event risk, and options-expiration effects.

DX-Y.NYB.translations.en.description: An index measuring the U.S. dollar against a basket of major currencies.
DX-Y.NYB.translations.en.market_role: It summarizes broad dollar strength and global liquidity pressure.
DX-Y.NYB.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher index indicates a stronger dollar, often tightening conditions for global risk assets.
DX-Y.NYB.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower index indicates a weaker dollar, often easing pressure on non-U.S. assets.
DX-Y.NYB.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with U.S. yields, EUR/USD, USD/JPY, commodities, and risk sentiment.

CL=F.translations.en.description: The front-month futures price for West Texas Intermediate crude oil.
CL=F.translations.en.market_role: It is a key signal for energy prices, inflation pressure, and global demand expectations.
CL=F.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher price can reflect stronger demand, supply disruption, or inflation pressure.
CL=F.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower price can reflect weaker demand, higher supply, or easing inflation pressure.
CL=F.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with Brent, the dollar, inventory data, geopolitical risk, and energy-sector performance.

GC=F.translations.en.description: The front-month futures price for gold.
GC=F.translations.en.market_role: Gold is watched as a real-rate, dollar, and safe-haven sensitive asset.
GC=F.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher price can signal stronger safe-haven demand, lower real yields, or a weaker dollar.
GC=F.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower price can signal higher real yields, a stronger dollar, or reduced defensive demand.
GC=F.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with real yields, DXY, inflation expectations, and risk sentiment.

HG=F.translations.en.description: The front-month futures price for copper.
HG=F.translations.en.market_role: Copper is a cyclical commodity often used as a gauge of industrial demand.
HG=F.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher price can signal stronger manufacturing or infrastructure demand.
HG=F.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower price can signal weaker industrial demand or stronger supply pressure.
HG=F.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with China data, manufacturing PMIs, the dollar, and the copper/gold ratio.

USDKRW.translations.en.description: The exchange rate between the U.S. dollar and the Korean won.
USDKRW.translations.en.market_role: It is important for Korean investors because it affects imported inflation, foreign flows, and global risk sensitivity.
USDKRW.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher rate means a stronger dollar or weaker won, often linked to risk-off pressure.
USDKRW.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower rate means a stronger won or weaker dollar, often linked to improved risk appetite.
USDKRW.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with DXY, U.S. yields, KOSPI, China data, and foreign investor flows.

EURUSD.translations.en.description: The exchange rate between the euro and the U.S. dollar.
EURUSD.translations.en.market_role: It is the main currency pair for comparing euro-area and U.S. macro expectations.
EURUSD.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher rate means a stronger euro or weaker dollar.
EURUSD.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower rate means a weaker euro or stronger dollar.
EURUSD.translations.en.watch_points: Watch U.S.-Europe rate differentials, ECB and Fed guidance, DXY, and energy-market pressures.

USDJPY.translations.en.description: The exchange rate between the U.S. dollar and the Japanese yen.
USDJPY.translations.en.market_role: It reflects rate differentials, dollar strength, and yen funding conditions.
USDJPY.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher rate means a stronger dollar or weaker yen.
USDJPY.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower rate means a weaker dollar or stronger yen.
USDJPY.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with U.S. yields, Bank of Japan expectations, Nikkei performance, and risk sentiment.

COPPER_GOLD.translations.en.description: A ratio comparing copper prices with gold prices.
COPPER_GOLD.translations.en.market_role: It is used as a rough gauge of cyclical growth appetite versus defensive demand.
COPPER_GOLD.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher ratio suggests stronger cyclical or industrial-demand sentiment.
COPPER_GOLD.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower ratio suggests more defensive demand or weaker growth expectations.
COPPER_GOLD.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with Treasury yields, China data, manufacturing indicators, and equity cyclicals.

WTI_BRENT_SPREAD.translations.en.description: The price difference between WTI crude and Brent crude.
WTI_BRENT_SPREAD.translations.en.market_role: It helps identify relative U.S. versus global crude-market tightness.
WTI_BRENT_SPREAD.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher spread can mean WTI is strengthening versus Brent or the discount is narrowing.
WTI_BRENT_SPREAD.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower spread can mean WTI is weakening versus Brent or the discount is widening.
WTI_BRENT_SPREAD.translations.en.watch_points: Check inventory data, export constraints, geopolitics, refinery demand, and the overall oil-price trend.

XLK.translations.en.description: A U.S. equity sector ETF proxy for technology companies.
XLK.translations.en.market_role: It shows leadership or weakness in technology shares within the broader market.
XLK.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise suggests stronger demand for technology and growth exposure.
XLK.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline suggests weaker technology sentiment or pressure from rates and earnings.
XLK.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with NASDAQ, 10-year yields, semiconductors, and earnings revisions.

XLF.translations.en.description: A U.S. equity sector ETF proxy for banks, insurers, and financial companies.
XLF.translations.en.market_role: It reflects credit conditions, yield-curve expectations, and financial-sector sentiment.
XLF.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise can signal stronger confidence in banks, credit, or net-interest-margin expectations.
XLF.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline can signal concern about credit quality, curve pressure, or financial stress.
XLF.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with yield-curve slope, credit spreads, bank earnings, and regulatory news.

XLE.translations.en.description: A U.S. equity sector ETF proxy for energy companies.
XLE.translations.en.market_role: It tracks equity-market exposure to oil, gas, and energy-cycle expectations.
XLE.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise often reflects stronger energy prices or improved energy-sector sentiment.
XLE.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline often reflects weaker commodity prices or demand concerns.
XLE.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with WTI, Brent, the dollar, inventories, and geopolitical risk.

XLV.translations.en.description: A U.S. equity sector ETF proxy for health care companies.
XLV.translations.en.market_role: It is often viewed as a defensive sector with policy and earnings-specific drivers.
XLV.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise can indicate defensive demand or stronger sector fundamentals.
XLV.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline can indicate rotation away from defensives or sector-specific pressure.
XLV.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with broad equity sentiment, policy risk, earnings, and factor rotation.

XLI.translations.en.description: A U.S. equity sector ETF proxy for industrial companies.
XLI.translations.en.market_role: It reflects cyclical growth, capital spending, and manufacturing expectations.
XLI.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise suggests stronger cyclical and industrial demand expectations.
XLI.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline suggests weaker manufacturing or capital-spending sentiment.
XLI.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with ISM data, durable goods, copper, yields, and global trade indicators.

XLY.translations.en.description: A U.S. equity sector ETF proxy for consumer discretionary companies.
XLY.translations.en.market_role: It reflects consumer confidence, spending appetite, and growth-stock exposure.
XLY.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise suggests stronger discretionary spending expectations or risk appetite.
XLY.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline suggests consumer caution, rate pressure, or weaker growth expectations.
XLY.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with retail sales, labor data, consumer sentiment, rates, and earnings.

XLP.translations.en.description: A U.S. equity sector ETF proxy for consumer staples companies.
XLP.translations.en.market_role: It is often used as a defensive equity-sector benchmark.
XLP.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise can reflect defensive demand or stable earnings preference.
XLP.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline can reflect rotation toward cyclicals or sector-specific weakness.
XLP.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with XLY, inflation data, margins, and broad risk appetite.

XLU.translations.en.description: A U.S. equity sector ETF proxy for utility companies.
XLU.translations.en.market_role: It is rate-sensitive and often treated as a defensive, dividend-oriented sector.
XLU.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise can indicate defensive demand or lower-yield support.
XLU.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline can indicate higher-rate pressure or rotation into cyclicals.
XLU.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with Treasury yields, dividend factors, risk sentiment, and power-demand trends.

XLB.translations.en.description: A U.S. equity sector ETF proxy for materials companies.
XLB.translations.en.market_role: It reflects demand for chemicals, metals, construction inputs, and global cyclical activity.
XLB.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise suggests stronger cyclical or commodity-linked demand expectations.
XLB.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline suggests weaker global growth or commodity demand expectations.
XLB.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with copper, China data, manufacturing indicators, and the dollar.

XLRE.translations.en.description: A U.S. equity sector ETF proxy for real estate companies and REITs.
XLRE.translations.en.market_role: It is sensitive to interest rates, financing costs, and property-market expectations.
XLRE.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise can indicate lower-rate support or stronger property-sector sentiment.
XLRE.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline can indicate higher-rate pressure or concern about real-estate fundamentals.
XLRE.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with 10-year yields, credit conditions, housing data, and dividend factors.

XLC.translations.en.description: A U.S. equity sector ETF proxy for communication services companies.
XLC.translations.en.market_role: It includes media, telecom, and large platform businesses with growth and advertising exposure.
XLC.translations.en.higher_meaning: A rise suggests stronger demand for communication-platform and media exposure.
XLC.translations.en.lower_meaning: A decline suggests weaker growth, advertising, or platform-sector sentiment.
XLC.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with NASDAQ, technology shares, advertising trends, yields, and earnings.

fomc_next_meeting.translations.en.description: The date of the next Federal Open Market Committee meeting that will set the policy-rate decision and guidance.
fomc_next_meeting.translations.en.market_role: It anchors the timing of policy expectations across rates, FX, equities, and bonds.
fomc_next_meeting.translations.en.higher_meaning: For a date field, the key signal is not high or low but how close the meeting is and how expectations change before it.
fomc_next_meeting.translations.en.lower_meaning: For a date field, the key signal is not high or low but how close the meeting is and how expectations change before it.
fomc_next_meeting.translations.en.watch_points: Around the meeting, track FedWatch probabilities, 2-year yields, statement wording, and press-conference guidance.

fomc_decision_rate.translations.en.description: The policy-rate level decided at an FOMC meeting.
fomc_decision_rate.translations.en.market_role: It allows markets to compare the actual policy decision with expectations priced before the meeting.
fomc_decision_rate.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher-than-expected decision is generally a hawkish surprise and can tighten financial conditions.
fomc_decision_rate.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower-than-expected decision is generally a dovish surprise and can support liquidity expectations.
fomc_decision_rate.translations.en.watch_points: The rate level should be read together with the statement, dot plot, press conference, and forward guidance.

fomc_change_bp.translations.en.description: The size of the policy-rate change at the meeting, measured in basis points.
fomc_change_bp.translations.en.market_role: It captures the intensity of the policy move and the surprise versus market expectations.
fomc_change_bp.translations.en.higher_meaning: A larger hike or smaller cut than expected can be interpreted as a hawkish surprise.
fomc_change_bp.translations.en.lower_meaning: A larger cut or smaller hike than expected can be interpreted as a dovish surprise.
fomc_change_bp.translations.en.watch_points: Clearly define the sign convention in the UI and compare with pre-meeting FedWatch pricing.

fedwatch_prob_hold.translations.en.description: The market-implied probability that the Fed keeps the policy rate unchanged at a target meeting.
fedwatch_prob_hold.translations.en.market_role: It summarizes rate-market expectations before FOMC decisions.
fedwatch_prob_hold.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher probability indicates stronger expectations for no policy-rate change.
fedwatch_prob_hold.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower probability indicates rising expectations for a cut or hike instead of a hold.
fedwatch_prob_hold.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with 2-year yields, inflation data, labor data, and Fed communication.

fedwatch_prob_cut.translations.en.description: The market-implied probability that the Fed cuts the policy rate at a target meeting.
fedwatch_prob_cut.translations.en.market_role: It tracks how strongly markets expect policy easing.
fedwatch_prob_cut.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher probability signals stronger expectations for easier policy.
fedwatch_prob_cut.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower probability signals reduced expectations for easing.
fedwatch_prob_cut.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with inflation surprises, labor-market weakness, recession risk, and FOMC communication.

fedwatch_prob_hike.translations.en.description: The market-implied probability that the Fed raises the policy rate at a target meeting.
fedwatch_prob_hike.translations.en.market_role: It tracks how strongly markets expect policy tightening.
fedwatch_prob_hike.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher probability signals stronger expectations for tighter policy.
fedwatch_prob_hike.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower probability signals reduced expectations for additional tightening.
fedwatch_prob_hike.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with inflation pressure, wage data, 2-year yields, and FOMC communication.

US_CPI.translations.en.description: A major inflation release that measures changes in prices paid by consumers for goods and services.
US_CPI.translations.en.market_role: Markets watch CPI because high inflation can reduce rate-cut expectations and pressure risk assets.
US_CPI.translations.en.higher_meaning: A stronger-than-expected release can be read as persistent inflation pressure and may push yields higher.
US_CPI.translations.en.lower_meaning: A weaker-than-expected release can be read as easing inflation pressure and may support easier-policy expectations.
US_CPI.translations.en.watch_points: Focus on core CPI, shelter, services inflation, and the immediate reaction in 2-year yields, the dollar, and equity futures.

US_PPI.translations.en.description: A producer-price release that measures price changes faced by businesses at the production stage.
US_PPI.translations.en.market_role: It helps markets assess whether upstream cost pressure may pass through to consumer inflation.
US_PPI.translations.en.higher_meaning: A stronger-than-expected release can raise concern about future inflation pressure.
US_PPI.translations.en.lower_meaning: A weaker-than-expected release can suggest easing cost pressure for businesses.
US_PPI.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with CPI, commodity prices, Treasury yields, and dollar moves.

US_PCE.translations.en.display_name: U.S. PCE Inflation / Personal Income and Outlays
US_PCE.translations.en.description: A release covering the Fed-preferred PCE inflation measures together with personal income and spending.
US_PCE.translations.en.market_role: Core PCE is closely tied to Fed policy assessment, so markets react strongly to surprises.
US_PCE.translations.en.higher_meaning: A stronger-than-expected release can make the Fed less confident that inflation is cooling.
US_PCE.translations.en.lower_meaning: A weaker-than-expected release can improve confidence that inflation is moving toward target.
US_PCE.translations.en.watch_points: Focus on core PCE, income, spending momentum, revisions, FedWatch pricing, and the yield-curve reaction.

US_EMPLOYMENT_SITUATION.translations.en.description: The main U.S. labor-market release covering nonfarm payrolls, unemployment, and wage growth.
US_EMPLOYMENT_SITUATION.translations.en.market_role: It can change expectations for growth, inflation, and the Fed policy path.
US_EMPLOYMENT_SITUATION.translations.en.higher_meaning: Stronger job or wage data can signal resilient demand and potential inflation pressure.
US_EMPLOYMENT_SITUATION.translations.en.lower_meaning: Weaker job or wage data can signal labor-market cooling and slower growth.
US_EMPLOYMENT_SITUATION.translations.en.watch_points: Read payrolls, unemployment, participation, average hourly earnings, revisions, and the reaction in yields and equities together.

US_JOBLESS_CLAIMS.translations.en.description: A weekly release showing first-time filings for unemployment insurance.
US_JOBLESS_CLAIMS.translations.en.market_role: It is one of the timeliest indicators of labor-market stress.
US_JOBLESS_CLAIMS.translations.en.higher_meaning: A higher-than-expected reading can point to rising layoffs and weaker labor demand.
US_JOBLESS_CLAIMS.translations.en.lower_meaning: A lower-than-expected reading can point to resilient labor demand.
US_JOBLESS_CLAIMS.translations.en.watch_points: Use the four-week average and compare with the unemployment rate, payroll trend, yields, and equity reaction.

US_JOLTS.translations.en.description: A labor-market release covering job openings, quits, hires, and separations.
US_JOLTS.translations.en.market_role: It helps markets assess labor demand and wage-pressure risks beyond payrolls.
US_JOLTS.translations.en.higher_meaning: A stronger-than-expected reading can indicate tight labor conditions.
US_JOLTS.translations.en.lower_meaning: A weaker-than-expected reading can indicate cooling labor demand.
US_JOLTS.translations.en.watch_points: Focus on job openings, quits, revisions, and consistency with claims, unemployment, and wage data.

US_GDP.translations.en.description: A broad release measuring the inflation-adjusted value of goods and services produced in the U.S. economy.
US_GDP.translations.en.market_role: It is the main benchmark for overall growth momentum.
US_GDP.translations.en.higher_meaning: A stronger-than-expected release can signal resilient growth and support cyclical assets, but may also affect rate expectations.
US_GDP.translations.en.lower_meaning: A weaker-than-expected release can signal growth slowdown and increase defensive demand.
US_GDP.translations.en.watch_points: Look at real final sales, consumption, inventories, inflation components, revisions, yields, and equity leadership.

US_RETAIL_SALES.translations.en.description: A monthly release tracking sales by retailers and providing a timely view of consumer spending.
US_RETAIL_SALES.translations.en.market_role: It is important because consumption is a large part of U.S. economic activity.
US_RETAIL_SALES.translations.en.higher_meaning: A stronger-than-expected release can signal resilient consumer demand.
US_RETAIL_SALES.translations.en.lower_meaning: A weaker-than-expected release can signal consumer caution or slowing demand.
US_RETAIL_SALES.translations.en.watch_points: Focus on the control group, revisions, inflation effects, consumer discretionary shares, and rates.

US_DURABLE_GOODS.translations.en.description: A release measuring new orders for long-lasting manufactured goods.
US_DURABLE_GOODS.translations.en.market_role: It helps assess business investment, manufacturing demand, and cyclical momentum.
US_DURABLE_GOODS.translations.en.higher_meaning: A stronger-than-expected release can indicate improving capital-spending and manufacturing demand.
US_DURABLE_GOODS.translations.en.lower_meaning: A weaker-than-expected release can indicate softer business investment or manufacturing momentum.
US_DURABLE_GOODS.translations.en.watch_points: Watch core capital-goods orders, aircraft volatility, revisions, industrials, copper, and yields.

US_HOUSING_STARTS.translations.en.description: A monthly release showing the number of new residential construction projects started.
US_HOUSING_STARTS.translations.en.market_role: It is a rate-sensitive indicator of housing activity and construction momentum.
US_HOUSING_STARTS.translations.en.higher_meaning: A stronger-than-expected release can suggest resilient housing demand or construction activity.
US_HOUSING_STARTS.translations.en.lower_meaning: A weaker-than-expected release can suggest pressure from mortgage rates or slower housing demand.
US_HOUSING_STARTS.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with permits, mortgage-rate proxies, 10-year yields, homebuilder sentiment, and real-estate equities.

US_NEW_HOME_SALES.translations.en.description: A monthly release showing sales of newly built single-family homes.
US_NEW_HOME_SALES.translations.en.market_role: It provides a read on housing demand and household confidence in a rate-sensitive sector.
US_NEW_HOME_SALES.translations.en.higher_meaning: A stronger-than-expected release can signal resilient housing demand.
US_NEW_HOME_SALES.translations.en.lower_meaning: A weaker-than-expected release can signal affordability pressure or weaker housing activity.
US_NEW_HOME_SALES.translations.en.watch_points: Compare with mortgage-rate proxies, housing starts, homebuilder sentiment, 10-year yields, and real-estate equities.

US_ISM_MANUFACTURING.translations.en.description: A survey-based indicator of U.S. manufacturing activity.
US_ISM_MANUFACTURING.translations.en.market_role: It is watched for early signals on cyclical growth, orders, prices, and employment.
US_ISM_MANUFACTURING.translations.en.higher_meaning: A stronger-than-expected release can indicate improving manufacturing momentum.
US_ISM_MANUFACTURING.translations.en.lower_meaning: A weaker-than-expected release can indicate contracting or slowing manufacturing conditions.
US_ISM_MANUFACTURING.translations.en.watch_points: Focus on new orders, prices paid, employment, inventories, industrials, copper, and yields.

US_ISM_SERVICES.translations.en.description: A survey-based indicator of U.S. services-sector activity.
US_ISM_SERVICES.translations.en.market_role: Services drive a large share of the U.S. economy and inflation pressure.
US_ISM_SERVICES.translations.en.higher_meaning: A stronger-than-expected release can signal resilient demand and possible services inflation pressure.
US_ISM_SERVICES.translations.en.lower_meaning: A weaker-than-expected release can signal cooling demand in the services sector.
US_ISM_SERVICES.translations.en.watch_points: Focus on business activity, new orders, employment, prices paid, yields, and equity-sector reaction.

FOMC_MEETING.translations.en.description: A Federal Reserve policy meeting where the committee sets the policy-rate decision and communicates its outlook.
FOMC_MEETING.translations.en.market_role: It is one of the most important events for rates, FX, equities, and credit markets.
FOMC_MEETING.translations.en.higher_meaning: A more hawkish decision or message can tighten financial conditions.
FOMC_MEETING.translations.en.lower_meaning: A more dovish decision or message can ease financial conditions.
FOMC_MEETING.translations.en.watch_points: Compare the decision with FedWatch pricing, statement wording, dot plot, press conference, and moves in 2-year yields.

FOMC_MINUTES.translations.en.description: The detailed record of a previous FOMC meeting's discussion.
FOMC_MINUTES.translations.en.market_role: It helps markets interpret the committee's reaction function and balance of risks.
FOMC_MINUTES.translations.en.higher_meaning: More hawkish minutes can raise expected policy restrictiveness.
FOMC_MINUTES.translations.en.lower_meaning: More dovish minutes can lower expected policy restrictiveness.
FOMC_MINUTES.translations.en.watch_points: Watch language on inflation, labor markets, financial conditions, balance sheet policy, and the reaction in yields and the dollar.

US_MONTHLY_OPEX.translations.en.description: The monthly expiration of listed options contracts, often concentrated on the third Friday of the month.
US_MONTHLY_OPEX.translations.en.market_role: It can affect short-term equity index flows, hedging demand, and volatility around expiration.
US_MONTHLY_OPEX.translations.en.higher_meaning: A larger expiration with strong dealer-positioning effects can amplify short-term moves.
US_MONTHLY_OPEX.translations.en.lower_meaning: A smaller or less concentrated expiration may have a more limited market impact.
US_MONTHLY_OPEX.translations.en.watch_points: Track S&P 500, NASDAQ, VIX, index levels versus large option strikes, and post-expiration liquidity.

US_TRIPLE_WITCHING.translations.en.description: A quarterly expiration date when stock options, stock-index futures, and stock-index options expire together.
US_TRIPLE_WITCHING.translations.en.market_role: It can increase volume, rebalance flows, and short-term volatility in equity markets.
US_TRIPLE_WITCHING.translations.en.higher_meaning: Large positioning into expiration can amplify index or sector moves.
US_TRIPLE_WITCHING.translations.en.lower_meaning: Light positioning or offsetting flows can reduce the visible market impact.
US_TRIPLE_WITCHING.translations.en.watch_points: Watch S&P 500, NASDAQ, VIX, sector ETFs, futures rolls, and closing-auction volume.

US_CONSUMER_SENTIMENT.translations.en.description: A survey release measuring households' views on current conditions, expectations, and inflation.
US_CONSUMER_SENTIMENT.translations.en.market_role: It helps markets assess consumer confidence and inflation expectations.
US_CONSUMER_SENTIMENT.translations.en.higher_meaning: A stronger-than-expected release can signal resilient consumer confidence.
US_CONSUMER_SENTIMENT.translations.en.lower_meaning: A weaker-than-expected release can signal consumer caution or weaker spending intentions.
US_CONSUMER_SENTIMENT.translations.en.watch_points: Focus on inflation-expectations components, current conditions, expectations, retail sales, and consumer-discretionary stocks.
